## 48bda9528e71

### A2: Reproduced domain coverage gap — convexifying before outlining remains indistinguishable on generated inputs

**Finding:** The current sampler cannot distinguish the stated row/column-extent transformation from an independent rival that first fills the integer lattice points in the occupied cells' Euclidean convex hull, then draws its exterior cardinal-neighbor shell. The rival matches all three unique canonical pairs and all 60 generated inputs tested. It disagrees with Racket on a small input that passes the task's validator and satisfies its documented invariants. This is a reproduced distribution/domain coverage issue and a possible learning shortcut; no incorrect Racket label or measured model learning failure is claimed. This audit changed no generator or rule.

The decisive evidence is [counterexample.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/counterexample.json). The independent implementation, complete sample manifest, and measured results are in [probe.py](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/probe.py), [sampling.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/sampling.json), and [summary.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/summary.json).

### Bound source and prior leads

The audited generator is version `2.0.0`, SHA-256 `102426f4ed3df872c33fa261f413057e45ceedbfa5e662b82a3017b56887e9cc`. The selected canonical rule ID is `b9f9e9bda3f3`; its full whitespace-normalized source SHA-256 is `b9f9e9bda3f360c20aa772dfedc3adc436e725f5f33659fc056cee0312ee293f`. The exact, unnormalized canonical source SHA-256 is `cbaac000ae7b97165d8b2427d8fc2bc87387647706d8a68e87b1d2f5ff95c4db`.

The public Racket receipt independently records the same generator and rule identities, and executed callable SHA-256 `d637b70db56a5ef96583b65078905fc8fd18f7ca3fef08dc1dc41b25e63f1020`. The callable and full `(rule! ...)` source are different representations and their hashes are retained separately.

Retained notes `GNOTE-000899` (accepted rule), `GNOTE-000979` (lawful orthogonally convex generalization; source return `k12/RESULTS.json`), and `GNOTE-000865` (generalized-branch limitations; source return `h00/RESULTS.json`) were leads. Their earlier counts and acceptance claims were not treated as measurements of this source. No private solve material was consulted.

### Concrete accepted witness

Use a `9x9` grid with background `8`. Paint color `4` in rows `2..4`, columns `2..6`, and rows `5..6`, columns `2..4`; replace cell `(3,3)` by color `2`. All coordinates in this section are zero-based. This is an L-shaped occupied region with a concave corner.

The input has 21 occupied cells: color `4` occurs 20 times, color `2` once, and background `8` 60 times. It is 4-connected; each occupied row and column is contiguous; the rare cell has all four occupied cardinal neighbors. It spans five rows and columns and exposes 19 in-bounds extent markers. These facts satisfy every `INVARIANTS` entry and every executable `self_check` constraint. The actual validator returned `[]`, and `observe_overrides` returned `{"grid_size": 9, "scene_profile": "general"}`.

Convexification adds exactly cell `(5,5)`. The real Racket transformation marks `(5,5)` with `2`, because it lies just beyond both an occupied row and an occupied column. The rival makes this cell part of the convexified interior, so outputs `8` there. The two complete outputs differ at **exactly this one cell**. The input and both full output grids are retained in the counterexample file; its index in the batch is `63`, with no seed or sample index because it was constructed explicitly.

The witness belongs to the documented and validator-accepted grammar. It is **outside the actual sampler's current support**, which is the issue being demonstrated; it is not presented as a generated counterexample.

### Why the shortcut survives the sampler

In `_general_mask`, an occupied mask is the set of integer points in a rectangle intersected with four closed diagonal half-planes. If this convex polygon is `P` and its occupied lattice-point set is `S = P ∩ Z²`, then `S ⊆ conv(S) ∩ Z² ⊆ P ∩ Z² = S`. Thus taking its convex hull cannot add any integer cells. Translation and all subsequent validity filters preserve the property.

The three canonical masks were checked independently: their occupied-cell counts are 12, 16, and 25, and each also contains every integer point in its convex hull. D4 symmetry and nonbackground color renaming preserve occupancy and this property. Consequently the extra convexification step is unobservable throughout the successful outputs of both current generation branches. Here “convex” refers to the lattice-point set, not to the union of square pixels as a continuous region.

For an orthogonally convex mask, its exterior four-neighbor shell equals the reference's row/column-extent markers: every missing horizontal neighbor is beyond a row endpoint, and every missing vertical neighbor is beyond a column endpoint. This proves the rival's agreement with the documented transformation on the sampler's support. The executions below establish actual Racket agreement on the retained cases. No universal empirical claim is made from 60 samples.

### Focused measurements and commands

The batch contained all three unique canonical input/output pairs, 60 actual `generate` calls, and the one constructed witness. Generated inputs used **each difficulty band** `easy`, `medium`, and `hard`, **seeds `0..19` per band**, `sample_index = 17 * seed + 3`, and the exact override `{"scene_profile": "general"}`. There was no audit-side rejection or filtering. All 60 generated inputs were distinct; all 64 batch inputs were distinct. Both canonical records were read, yielding six pairs and three unique pairs. The generator declares neither `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` nor `LESSON_COMPETITORS`; this audit supplied the independent rival and did not claim a lesson-contract result.

| Check | Measured result |
|---|---:|
| Task validator accepts batch inputs | 64/64 |
| Racket applications succeed | 64/64, zero per-input errors |
| Racket agrees with stored canonical labels | 3/3 unique pairs |
| Convexify-then-shell rival agrees with canonical labels and Racket | 3/3 unique pairs |
| Rival agrees with generated Racket outputs | 60/60 unique inputs |
| Convexification changes generated occupied masks | 0/60 |
| Rival disagrees on constructed accepted witness | 1/1 |
| Independent cardinal shell without convexification agrees with Racket | 64/64 |

The reference was obtained exclusively through the supported command, run from `packet_root`:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 48bda9528e71 --input ../checks/audit/48bda9528e71/input.json --out ../checks/audit/48bda9528e71/racket.json
```

It exited `0`; the wrapper's effective working directory was `repo`. [command_receipt.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/command_receipt.json) retains the exact argument array, both working directories, exit code, and output streams. [racket.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/racket.json) retains the actual outputs and source/input/output hashes; [rival.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/rival.json) retains all independent rival outputs.

The final comparison command was `python3 checks/audit/48bda9528e71/probe.py summarize`, from `packet_root`, exit `0`; its receipt is [summary_command_receipt.json](checks/audit/48bda9528e71/summary_command_receipt.json). In a fresh copy without existing evidence outputs, `python3 checks/audit/48bda9528e71/probe.py` prepares the inputs, executes the public command, and summarizes the audit.

The initial audit harness exited `1` after the successful Racket batch because it incorrectly equated full-source and executable-callable hashes. The initial script and failure are retained as `probe_initial.py` and `probe_initial_receipt.json`. Correcting that bookkeeping assertion did not change any input, generator, rule, rival, or Racket result. The final comparison consumed the retained successful Racket output; no extra reference run was needed.

### Scope and suggested disposition

This was a focused adversarial audit, without a full battery, lesson-frequency census, or model evaluation. The source argument identifies a real restriction, while the witness makes its consequence reproducible. If the documented orthogonally convex grammar is the intended teaching domain, adding occasional concave-but-orthogonally-convex masks would distinguish this rival; otherwise the narrower supported domain should be stated explicitly. Neither a fix nor a change in admission status was made by this audit.

triage.reason: Short brief and general feedback read under one-minute policy; routine source repair accepted as reviewer-reported. Complete-lesson/replay/override proposals retained; durable output and portable-test subset already implemented. Both audits and unscored solves retained; no training admission.

findings.text:
## 48bda9528e71

**Reproduced domain restriction: convexification shortcut.** A rival that fills
the orthogonal convex hull of the selected mask matches **300/300 accepted
generated inputs** (100 per easy/medium/hard) from final source hash
`102426f4ed3df872c33fa261f413057e45ceedbfa5e662b82a3017b56887e9cc`.
Convexification changes the generated mask in 0/300 cases, so the sampler never
teaches that concavities should be preserved.

A lawful accepted 9×9 concave witness breaks the shortcut at `(5,5)`: intended
output color 2, rival color 8. The selected Racket output is valid, matches the
independent mirror, and differs from the rival. Reproducer and hashes:
`checks/audit/48bda9528e71/{input.json,racket.json,rival.json,counterexample.json,summary.json}`.

This is an audit-only finding; the target source was not edited.

resolution_reason: Convexification rival repaired: v2.1 guarantees two concave witnesses in every four-slot production cycle, preserving one under every single query holdout. Retained actual-Racket counterexamples and reported rotated/fixed-period evidence cover this named rival. The prior orthogonal-hull wording is corrected in current notes: the implemented shortcut was Euclidean hull.
